primary_claim: Varying the ratio of addition to multiplication problems in training data shifts the timing of grokking (local learning coefficient decline) toward whichever operation dominates, but does not produce separate, distinct developmental stages in the LLC curve for each operation, contrary to the author's hypothesis.

effect.metric: local learning coefficient (LLC) curve shape / stage separation across addition:multiplication training ratios
effect.value: no distinct additional developmental stages observed; a single LLC decline across all ratios tested (30-70% addition), though the decline's onset timing shifted earlier for more uneven ratios

contradicts_or_qualifies: Author's initial hypothesis, drawing on developmental interpretability framing, was that different grokking rates for addition vs. multiplication would create noticeably separate developmental stages visible in the LLC; the data did not support this
stated_future_work: Investigate the cause of training loss-spike instability, possibly the 'slingshot mechanism' described in prior work
Create a multi-problem grokking scenario without loss spikes to collect cleaner LLC data that might yield different conclusions

Apply mechanistic interpretability techniques (as in Progress Measures for Grokking) to see how the addition and multiplication algorithms co-exist within the model, compared to single-operation training
limitations_stated: Data from the experiments was plagued with noise attributed at least partially to loss spikes during training
LLC estimation is very sensitive to the hyperparameters used to compute the estimates
Numerous techniques (hyperparameter combinations, learning rate schedulers, optimizers, layer normalization) were tried to remove training loss spikes but none succeeded
quote: the LLC curves did not reveal separate, distinct stages for learning addition versus multiplication, contrary to the initial hypothesis.
